title.narrative: Second Solomon Islands Roads and Aviation Project

description.narrative: The Second Solomon Islands Roads and Aviation Project (SIRAP2) was approved by the World Bank Board on June 1, 2022, with US$89.21 million equivalent IDA financing. A scale-up and cost overrun Additional Financing (AF1) for SIRAP2 was approved by the Management on February 21, 2025, with additional US$51.20 million IDA financing. The PDO of SIRAP2 is to “improve the climate resilience and safety of the Recipient's road and aviation sectors, and in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, respond promptly and effectively to it”. The proposed second Additional Financing (AF2) for SIRAP2 is for scale-up investments for replacing the Fiu River Bridge and upgrading and sealing of the two roads in Malaita Province as well as additional technical assistance to support the proposed AF2 activities.The PDO of SIRAP2 is expected to be achieved through the following four components:Component 1: Climate Resilience and Safety Investments in the Aviation Sector. This component finances the following activities: (a) improvements to Honiara International Airport in Guadalcanal Province, Munda International Airport in Western Province, Santa Cruz (Lata) Airfield in Temotu Province, and Suavanao Airfield in Isabel Province; (b) modernization of air navigation systems in Makira-Ulawa and Temotu Provinces; and (c) multiyear maintenance of critical mechanical and electrical assets at the two international airports.Component 2: Climate Resilience and Safety Investments in the Road Sector. This component finances climate resilience and safety improvements to 10 km of the road network in Noro in Western Province; the four bridges (Kolofe1, Kolofe2, Su’u Harbor, and Bira Brides) in Malaita Province, 12 km of North Road between Auki Gwaunaru’u Airfield and Kwaisulinin Road Junction, and 21 km of East Road between Baratoro and Atori in Malaita Province. The proposed AF2 will support to (i) replacing the Fiu River Bridge; (ii) upgrading of 7.4 km of the sealed roads between Auki Guwaunaru’u Airfield and Kilu’ufi Hospital Junction; and (iii) sealing of 5 km of the gravel road between Kwaisuliniu Road Junction and Dala Market in Malaita Province.Component 3: Institutional Strengthening and Project Management. This component finances technical assistance in the area of aviation planning, climate resilient transport, and road safety; and project implementation support in the form of a Project Support Team (PST). This component will also finance additional technical assistance activities (e.g., D&S consultancy, project management) under the proposed AF2.Component 4: Contingent Emergency Response. This zero-dollar component is designed to provide swift response in the event of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, by enabling SIG to request the World Bank to reallocate project funds to support emergency response and reconstruction.The proposed AF2 will fully be funded by IDA, with an estimated total cost of US$38 million, and no other donor investments are envisaged.
To improve the climate resilience and safety of the Recipient's road and aviation sectors, and in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, respond promptly and effectively to it.

condition.narrative: In order to carry out Part 1(e) of the Project, the Recipient shall enter into a Performance-Based Contract, with a private sectorcontractor selected on the basis of terms of reference, qualifications and experience satisfactory to the Association, inaccordancewith the provisions included or referred to in this Agreement (“PBC Contractor”), under terms and conditions acceptableto the Association. (Section I.B.1 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement)

The Recipient shall carry out, jointly with the Association, not later than three years after the Effective Date, or such otherperiod as may be agreed with the Association, a mid-term review of the Project to assess the status of Project implementation, asmeasured against the Project indicators acceptable to the Association, and compliance with the legal covenants. (Section II.2 ofSchedule 2 to the Financing Agreement)

The Recipient shall furnish to the Association each Project Report not later than forty-five (45) days after the end of eachcalendar quarter, covering the calendar quarter. (Section II.1 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement)

The Recipient shall maintain throughout Project implementation, the Project Support Team within the Ministry of Communication andAviation, with a mandate, composition and resources satisfactory to the Association, which shall: (a) be responsible for, interalia, day to day implementation of the Project including contract management, procurement, financial management, preparing and/orconsolidating Annual Work Plans and Budgets, technical aspects, environmental and social risks management, monitoring, reporting,and evaluation; (b) report to the focal point within the Ministry of Communication and Aviation and the focal point within theMinistry of Infrastructure Development; and (c) be comprised of, inter alia: (i) a project manager; (ii) a deputy project manager;(iii) a national safeguards officer; (iv) a community liaison officer; (v) a Project accountant; (vi) a procurement specialist;(vii) an administrative assistant; and (viii) a finance manager. (Section I.A.2 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement)

The Recipient shall prepare and furnish to the Association, by not later than November 30 of each year during the implementation ofthe Project, an Annual Work Plan and Budget for the Project. The Recipient shall ensure that the Project is implemented inaccordance with the Annual Work Plans and Budgets approved by the Association for the respective fiscal year. (Sections I.D.1 andI.D.2 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement)

The Recipient shall: (a) by not later than three months after the Effective Date, prepare and adopt a Project Operations Manual;and (b) thereafter ensure that the Project is carried out in accordance with the Project Operations Manual. (Section C.3 ofSchedule 2 to the Financing Agreement)

To ensure proper oversight of the Project at the national level, the Recipient shall maintain throughout Project implementation,the National Steering Committee, with a mandate, composition and resources satisfactory to the Association, which shall be: (a)responsible for, inter alia, providing Project oversight, approving Annual Work Plans and Budgets, and advising on Project relatedmatters; and (b) comprised of, inter alia: (i) Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Finance and Treasury (or his or herdesignee); (ii) the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Infrastructure Development (or his or her designee); (iii) the PermanentSecretary of the Ministry of Communication and Aviation (or his or her designee); (iv) the Provincial Secretary of Malaita Province(or his or her designee); (v) the Provincial Secretary of Western Province (or his or her designee); (vi) the Provincial Secretaryof Temotu Province (or his or her designee); and (vii) the Deputy Secretary – Technical of the Ministry of InfrastructureDevelopment (or his or her designee). (Section I.A.1 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement)

title.narrative: Successful implementation of agreed training plan for MCA, CAASI, SIACL, and Solomon Airlines

comment.narrative: Training plan was prepared for MCA, SIACL, CAASI, and Solomon Airlines through the training needs assessment under SIRAP. Based on the training needs assessment and the discussion with Solomon Airlines, it was agreed to use SIRAP2 funds to deliver Dash 8 type rating training course for their eight engineering staff. Web-based theorical training was provided from September 2-20, 2024, and the on-site practical training was provided in Honiara from September 23 to October 11, 2024. This enabled them to progress to licensed aircraft maintenance engineers who can sign off the aircraft after maintenance, and thus, can improve reliability of aircraft operations. Further training is currently being arranged (and undertaken) in consultation with MCA, SIACL, CAASI and Solomon Airlines.

title.narrative: Consultancy for detailed design and supervision of building and civil works provided

baseline.value: No contract with the consulting firm in place

target.value: Supervision of building and civil works completed with Defect Liability Period completed

comment.narrative: The contract with the SIRAP2 D&S consultant was executed on March 21, 2023. The design reports for all the key infrastructure investments under the original scope of SIRAP2 have been accepted, with the construction supervision of the Honiara Airport runway resurfacing, perimeter fence, standby generators, Noro Roads improvement, Santa Cruz Airfield upgrading, Malaita Bridges improvement, Honiara Airport rescue fire services station, Honiara and Munda Airports ATC tower, and Honiara Airport aviation complex building underway. The AF D&SS Phase I (Design) & II (Procurement Support) Effective Date is May 16, 2025 and services will continue through to February 15, 2026. The final Inception Report was issued on July 22, 2025, and the final Suavanao Airfield Design Review Report was issued on September 10, 2025. The AF D&SS Phase III (Construction Supervision) is expected to start in Q1 2026.

actual.value: The Design Reports for all the key infrastructure investments accepted, with the construction supervision of the Honiara Airport, Munda Airport, Santa Cruz Airfield, Noro Roads, and Malaita Bridges works underway.
